Guidelines for realizing loans by Banks  
*64     MS. MABEL REBELLO:                        
             SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA: 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government had issued guidelines against the banks whose agents have 
allegedly been found harassing the customers for realizing the loans; 
(b) if so, the details of the protection given to the customers and the agencies 
where such complaints for redressal could be lodged; 
(c) whether such guidelines put onus on the concerned banks; and 

6    Written Answers to [RAJYA SABHA]                    Starred Questions  
(d) if so, what steps have been taken against the b anks in the recent cases of 
harassment as reported in the media? 
THE MINISTER OF FINANCE (SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM): (a) To protect the 
rights of bank customers, prevent their harassment,  etc. steps taken by Government 
of India/Reserve Bank of India (RBI), inter-alia, include the following:— 
(i) RBI has issued instructions/guidelines to banks  on 'Managing Risks and 
Code of Conduct in Outsourcing of Financial Services'. 
(ii) RBI has formulated the "Fair Practices Code for Lenders". 
(iii) RBI has issued instructions to All Commercial  Banks/NBFCs (excluding 
RRBs) regarding Credit Card Operations. 
(iv) Further, the Code of Banks' Commitments to Cus tomers formulated by 
Banking Codes and Standard Board of India (BCSBI) provides, inter-alia, 
that the collection policy of the bank be built on courtesy, fair treatment 
and persuasion and the bank follows a security repo ssession policy in 
consonance with the law. 
(v) The Indian Banks Association (IBA) has formulat ed a "Model Code for 
collection of dues and repossession of security" as  also a "Fair Practice 
Code for credit card operations" which has been recommended to banks for 
adoption and implementation. 
(b) In case of violation of the said guidelines, the cu stomers aggrieved cim lodge 
complaints with RBI's Customer Service Department, Banking Division of Department 
of Financial Services, Public Grievances Cell of concerned banks, Banking Ombudsman 
and District Consumer Forum. Further, the aggrieved can also lodge complaints with 
local police. 
(c) The guidelines issued by RBI clearly stipulate that  the banks would be 
responsible for all acts of omission or commission of their agents. RBI reserves the 
right to impose penalty on a bank for violation of guidelines under the provision of 
Banking Regulation Act, 1949. 
(d) RBI takes up the complaints with the concerned bank s and cautions them to 
ensure that such incidences do not recur in future.  In the Mid-Term Review of 
Annual Policy Statement (dated October 30,2007), RBI has observed that in view of 
the rise in the number of litigations against banks for engaging recovery agents in the 
recent past, it is felt that the adverse publicity could result in serious reputational risk 
for the banking sector as a whole. RBI has urged banks to follow prescribed specific 
considerations while engaging recovery agents and h as clarified that complaints 
received regarding abusive practices followed by a bank's recovery agent would invite 
serious supervisory disapproval. RBI would consider  imposing a temporary ban (or 
even a permanent ban in case of persistent abusive practices) for engaging recovery 
agents on those banks where strictures have been passed/penalties have been-imposed 
by a High Court/Supreme Court or against its Direct ors/Officers with regard to the 
abusive practices followed by their recovery agents.

Criteria for price-fixation of gas from KG basin  
*66.     SHRI D. RAJA: 
 SHRI SYED AZEEZ PASHA: 
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether there have been concerns voiced by certain quarters about the pricing 
of natural gas to be extracted from Krishna-Godavar i (KG) basin by Reliance 
Industries Ltd.; 
(b) if so, what is the criteria adopted in fixing the p rices of natural gas being 
extracted by Reliance from KG basin; and 
(c) what is the Government's reaction to the concerns being expressed by certain 
quarters? 
THE MINISTER OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS (SHRI MUR LI 
DEORA): (a) to (c) Yes, Sir. The Production Sharing  Contract (PSC) provides for 
pricing of gas on the basis of sales on arms lengtkprinciples. The formula or basis on 
which the prices shall be determined for the purpos es of determining the 
Government take is required to be approved by the G overnment prior to sale of 
natural gas to the consumers/buyers. Accordingly, R IL submitted a proposal on 
18.5.07 for approval of gas price formula which was arrived at by following a bidding 
process. 
After taking into account the concerns voiced in some quarters regarding pricing of 
gas from KG Basin Block of RIL, the Government took the action of constituting an 
Empowered Group of Ministers (EGoM) to consider and  decide the issues of gas 
pricing and commercial utilization of gas under New  Exploration Licensing Policy 
(NELP). EGoM considered the price basis/formula submitted by RIL and decided the 
issue of pricing of gas under NELP.

Article 21.6.3 of the PSC for valuation of natural gas may be accepted with 
modifications.

(c) which of the States are in favour of imposing levy on commercial use of 
ground water; 
(d) whether the Prime Minister had advocated a holistic  approach to water 
conservation, instead of subsidizing it for economic and commercial use and hinted 
to "put the prices of water to save it"; and 
(e) it so, whether Government propose to launch a movem ent for water 
harvesting as a mission of conservation on a pattern adopted in Chennai? 
THE MINISTER OF WATER RESOURCES (PROF. SAIF-UD-DIN SOZ): (a) 
to (e) The National Congress on Ground Water was held on 11th September, 2007 at 
New Delhi. During the Congress, the discussion focu ssed on sustainable 
management of ground water. The need for strengthen ing awareness/education 
programmes and taking up of steps for enhancing wat er use efliciency was 
emphasised. The outcome of the Congress are given i n Statement (See below). The 
issue of levy on water was not discussed with the S tate Government during the 
Congress. 
The Prime Minister in his inaugural address stated that water is a national resource 
and an integrated view is to be taken of the countr y's water resources. The Prime 
Minister also emphasized the need for a paradigm sh ift in dealing with demand 
management as also on the importance of efficient, economic and more rational use 
of water. He opined that every living being has the  right to potable water. He called 
for economic use of water specially in irrigation, construction and other sectors and

Access to Finance for India's Rural Poor", has mentioned that some 66 per cent of large

farm yield and their income, emerging changes in so cial milieu and alienation of 
the individuals from family and society.

220. SHRI C. PERUMAL: Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have received any representation requesting removal of 
three per cent Central Sales Tax for Cotton on inter-State sale; 
(b) if so, whether Government have conceded such request of removal of Central 
Sales Tax for inter-State sale since the transport cost for those cotton is high 
comparing to overseas transportation; 
(c) if so, the details thereof; and .  
(d) if not, the reason therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE (S HRI S.S. 
PALANIMANICKAM): (a) No, Sir. 
(b) to (d) A consensus has been arrived at between the Government of India and 
the States to phase out Central Sales Tax (CST) on inter-State sale of goods by 
01.04.2000. As a first step, CST rate has been redu ced from 4% to 3% with effect 
from 01.04.2007. Further, it is stated that Section 8(5) of the Central Sales Tax Act, 
1956 empowers the respective State Government, if it is satisfied that it is necessary 
so to do in the public interest, to lower the tax r ate or exempt the tax-for sale in 
course of inter-State trade or commerce for any goo ds or class of goods from any 
particular place of business; or all sales of goods  or classes of goods by any dealer 
or by any class of dealers, to any person or class of persons-as may be notified by 
it.

223. SHRI JANARDHANA POOJARY: Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased 
to state:

and

education loans and home loans on low income and sa laried class borrowers and in 
respect of such borrowers whose children have availed education loans? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE (SHRI PAWAN 
KUMAR BANSAL): (a) to (c) The interest rates on adv ances are deregulated and 
banks are free to fix the rate of interest themselves with the approval of their Boards. 
Banks have been advised to fix their Benchmark Prim e Lending Rate (BPLR) after

242. SHRI N.R. GOVfNDARAJAR: Will the Minister of P ETROLEUM AND 
NATURAL GAS be pleasedlB state: 
(a) whether Directorate General of Hydro Carbons (DGH) have been empowered to 
oversee ever increasing exploration and production activities of private sector oil 
companies in the country; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) to what extent the DGH have cross checked the activities of private sector oil 
companies? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND 
NATURAL GAS (SHRI DINSHA J. PAEL): (a) and (b) Government has strengthened 
Directorate General of Hydrocarbons (DGH) to exercise certain powers and functions of 
Central Government with a view to promoting sound management of the hydrocarbon 
resources in the country in respect of exploratfon and production companies including public, 
private and foreign companies having balanced regar d for environmental, safety, 
technological and economic aspects.

Paradigm shift in water policy 
276. SHRIMATI SUPRIYA SULE: 
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA BHARTIA: 
Will the Minister of WATER RESOURCES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether scientists are concerned over the steady de cline in per capita water 
availability in the country and have called for pro per planning to reverse the 
negative trend; 
(b) whether in 1991, per capita fresh water availabilit y in the country was 2,209 
litre while it came down to only 1,820 litres in 2000 and by 2005, this is expected to 
further come down to only 1,341 litres; 
(c) whether these scientists have suggested that to ens ure availability of 
minimum fresh water to the people, there is an urge nt need for paradigm shift in 
water policy; and 
(d) whether Government have considered their suggestions? . 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESO URCES 
(SHRI JAY PRAKASH NARAYAN YADAV): (a) to (d) The average annual water 
availability in the country if assessed as 1869 Billion Cubic Metre (BCM) which may 
be considered to remain unchanged. The annual per c apita water availability in the 
country works out to be 2209 cubic metre as per the 1991 census. On the basis of the 
2001 census, the annual per capita water availabili ty has been estimated to 1820 
cubic metre and as per the projected population for  the year 2025, the annual per 
capita water availability is assessed as 1340 cubic metre. 
The scientists, researchers and planners have expressed concerns about the water 
resources scenario emerging due to population growt h, industrialization and 
urbanization from time to time at various fora. Sev eral research papers and 
recommendations of Seminar, Symposium, Conferences etc. have addressed these 
issues and numerous suggestions relating the need f or integrated and 
comprehensive planning for development, adoption of better management practices 
and implementation of efficient water management te chniques and water saving 
measures have been made. Observations/views have also been received in respect of 
National Water Policy (NWP) from various sources. T hese suggestions are duly 
examined and appropriately addressed. 
Measures for development and management of water re sources are undertaken 
by the respective State Governments which include c reation of storages through 
major, medium and minor irrigation projects, restoration of water bodies, rain water 
harvesting, artificial recharge to ground water ado ption of better management 
practices etc. Government of India provides necessa ry technical and fmancial 
assistance to the State Governments through various  schemes/ programmes. The 
Ministry of Water Resources encourage conservation of water including measures 
such as traditional water conservation practices, rainwater harvesting and recharge to 
ground water and adoption of better management practices.

277. SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRA SEKHAR: Will the Minister of WATER 
RESOURCES be pleased to state:

(SHRI JAY PRAKASH NARAYAN YADAV): (a) and (b) The M inistry of Water 
Resources (erstwhile Ministry of Irrigation) and Ce ntral Water Commission 
formulated a National Perspective Plan (NPP) for Wa ter Resources Development in 
1980. The NPP comprises of two components viz. (i) Peninsular Rivers Development 
and (ii) Himalayan Rivers Development and envisages  construction of storages on 
various river systems along with interlinking canal  systems to transfer water from 
water surplus areas to water deficit regions. Natio nal Water Development Agenpy 
(NWDA) was set up on 1982 to study the feasibility of Inter-basin water 
transfe«4>roposals and give a concrete shape to NPP . The Inter-linking propos .Is 
under NPP envisages additional benefits of 25 milli on ha. of irrigation from surface 
waters, 10 million ha. by increased use of ground w aters and generation of 34 
million KW of power apart from the incidental benef its of flood moderation, 
navigation, water supply, salinity and pollution control etc. 
Based on various studies conducted, NWDA has identi fied 30 links for 
preparation of feasibility Reports (FRs). Out of th ese, FRs of 14 links under 
Peninsular Component and 2 Links (Indian portion) u nder Himalayan Component 
have already been completed. NWDA has taken up the work of preparation of 
Detailed Project Report (DPR) for one priority link  viz. Ken-Betwa under 
Peninsular Component.

consensus and cooperation of the concerned States a nd agreements with the

284. SHRI MANOHAR JOSHI: Will the Minister of WATER  RESOURCES be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the State Government of M aharashtra has submitted a 
National Coastal Protection Project to get Central assistance; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether it is also a fact that proposals from five other State Governments are still 
pending; 
(d) if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) by when Government propose to take decision and rel ease the Central 
assistance to the said State Governments? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESO URCES 
(SHRI JAY PRAKASH NARAYAN YADAV): (a) to (e) Scheme s for anti-sea 
erosion works are planned and implemented by the re spective State Governments. 
Ministry of Water Resources has no scheme for providing Central assistance to States 
for coastal protection. However, realizing the impo rtance of such works, Central 
Water Commission requested the State Governments to  identify the critical reaches 
and submit suitable proposal with a view to prepare  a scheme namely National 
Coastal Protection Project (NCPP) for seeking exter nal funding. Proposals from 
various States including Maharashtra have been rece ived. Government of 
Maharashtra has submitted a proposal with an estima ted cost of Rs. 195.50 crore in 
July 2002 for inclusion in the National Coastal Pro tection Project (NCPP). The 
proposal includes construction of 72.36 km. of anti  erosion works in Mumbai, 
Mumbai Suburban, Thane, Raigad, Ratnagiri and Sindu durg Districts. The 
compliances to observations of Central Water Commis sion on the proposals 
submitted by the coastal States of Andhra Pradesh, Goa, Karnataka and Union 
Territory(UT) of Lakshadweep for inclusion in the NCPP have not been received. UT of 
Andaman and Nicobar Islands has not submitted any proposal. 
An Approach Paper prepared by Ministry of Water Resources on NCPP had been 
forwarded by Department of Economic Affairs (DEA) t o the Asian Development 
Bank (ADB) for consideration. ADB approved administ ering technical assistance 
to the Government of India for Technical Study on " Integrated Coastal Management 
and Related Investment Development". The Project Preparation Technical Assistance 
team in its report recommended Project Preparatory Technical Assistance (PPTA) to 
prepare a project/programme in 2007 having key comp onents for (i) institutional 
strengthening, capacity building and investment sup port for coastal management; 
(ii) capacity building and investment support for c oastal protection. Based on the 
recommendation of the PPTA, an ADB Fact Funding Mis sion visited three States 
namely Maharashtra, Goa and Karnataka during April-May, 2007. The Mission also 
recommended to work initially in Karnataka, Goa and  Maharashtra. Thereafter, a 
meeting was held in DEA and these three States have  been requested to confirm 
arrangement regarding mode of implementation of the project as a State sector project 
and that the fund from the ADB would be passed on t o the States on a back to back 
basis as is being done for all externally aided pro ject. The confirmation of 
Maharashtra Government has been received.

287.   SHRI BALAVANT  BAL APTE:  
SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS: 
Will the Minister of WATER RESOURCES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that information regarding thr ee lac square Km. water-
logged area in Sindhu region was known before the Indus Water Treaty-1960; 
(b) whether it is also a fact that India got only 9 to 10 per cent of this area; 
(c) whether there is no provision of review in the Treaty; 
(d) whether a demand for review can be made to safeguar d our national interests 
under Article 4 of the Helsinki Rules; and 
(e) if so, the details of the policy made thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESO URCES 
(SHRI JAY PRAKASH NARAYAN YADAV): (a) and (b) Avail able references 
indicate that water-logging in Sindhu region was known before the Indus Water Treaty 
1960. However, they do not provide any unique area of water-logging in Sindhu 
region and the area that India got. The report of t he Irrigation Commission - 1972 
states that about 10.9 lac hectares of area was aff ected in the Punjab State as 
estimated in the year 1958. Further, as per the boo k "The Indus Basin-History of 
Irrigation, Drainage and Flood Management" by CD. T hatte and Others, the 
survey in 1943 indicated that roughly an area of 0. 2 million ha. was affected by 
thur (alkali and saline soils) and sem (waterlogged) whereas the aerial 
reconnaissance survey got conducted by Government o f Pakistan in 1954 indicated 
that an area of more than 4.45 million ha. in West Pakistan was poorly drained and 
water-logged. 
(c) Relevant provisions of the Treaty (Article XII Final Provisions) which provide 
for its review are given below:— 
"(3)   The provisions of this Treaty may from time to time be modified by a duly 
ratified treat concluded for that purpose between the two Governments.  
(4) The provisions of this Treaty, or the provision s of this Treaty as modified 
under the provisions of Paragraph (3), shall contin ue in force until 
terminated by a duly ratified treaty concluded for that purpose between the 
two Governments".  
(d) The Helsinki Rules governing use of International W atercourses 1966 are 
guidelines adopted by the International Law Associa tion (ILA), a private body of 
lawyers are not binding upon States. 
(e) Does not arise.
